newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Reserve Bank sanguine on Gencor fx impact.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Reserve Bank sanguine on Gencor fx impact.

text.p: The South African Reserve Bank said on Tuesday it was comfortable with the exchange control implications of Gencor's planned transfer of non-precious metals assets to a U.K.-listed unit.

"You could look at it as circumventing (exchange controls) but..if this hadn't been done, Gencor might have been swallowed up by offshore investors and then dividend flows would have been one-way only," deputy governor James Cross told Reuters.
Gencor last week unveiled plans to list Billiton Plc in London and tap international markets for over $1 billion of equity capital in a move which had the blessing of the central Reserve Bank.
Some analysts said after the announcement that the deal would see sizeable dividend flows offshore, effectively liberalising exchange controls for Gencor.

"Dividends will be able to flow from South Africa to Billiton in hard currency and Billiton will then be able to do whatever it wishes with that money and that effectively gets round exchange controls," said a source close to the deal.

South African firms are currently prohibited from direct offshore investment unless they are institutions, execute asset swap transactions or structure a deal which offsets offshore flows, for example, by a boosting exports from South Africa.

The Reserve Bank's Cross noted dividend flows would also return to South Africa as a result of Gencor investor's holdings in Billiton which will be three Billiton shares and a letter of entitlement for every four Gencor shares.
"The idea is to allow the company to expand offshore without the exchange control brakes on those investments," he said.
Cross said the deal was part of South Africa's phased approach to removing corporate exchange controls.
